title: Check a budgets table before the model reads it

blocks.text: The budget model has one row per year and region, $`\text{spend}_{r,y} \le B_{r,y}`$ for every $`y \in Y`$ and $`r \in R`$, so it needs exactly one valid budget $`B_{r,y} \ge 0`$ for every pair, and nothing else. Finance sends the budgets as a CSV file with the columns `year`, `region` and `budget`, edited by hand.

Write `budget_problems(budgets, years, regions)` in `budgets.py`. `budgets` is the file read with `pd.read_csv` and no `dtype=`; `years` and `regions` are the plan's $`Y`$ and $`R`$. It returns one string per problem, in any order. Line numbers count the header as line 1, so the row with index 0 is line 2.

rows: `"line N: budget is not a number"`
the budget cell does not read as a number
another row has the same year and region (report every such row)
no row at all has year `Y` and region `R`

blocks.text: A row with a bad budget still counts as present for its year and region. An allowed table returns an empty list.

from __future__ import annotations

import pandas as pd


def budget_problems(budgets: pd.DataFrame, years: list[int], regions: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """One string per problem in a budgets table (see the statement's table)."""
    amount = pd.to_numeric(budgets["budget"], errors="coerce")
    rules = {
        "budget is not a number": amount.isna(),
        "negative budget": amount < 0,
        "unknown region": ~budgets["region"].isin(regions),
        "year outside the plan": ~budgets["year"].isin(years),
        "duplicate": budgets.duplicated(["year", "region"], keep=False),
    }
    problems = []
    for reason, mask in rules.items():
        problems += [f"line {n}: {reason}" for n in budgets.index[mask] + 2]
    present = set(zip(budgets["year"], budgets["region"]))
    problems += [f"missing {y} {r}" for y in years for r in regions if (y, r) not in present]
    return problems


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import io
    demo = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO("year,region,budget\n2031,North,500\n2031,North,-5\n"))
    print(budget_problems(demo, [2031], ["North", "South"]))

cases.says: a table with one valid row for every year and region has no problems
a negative budget is reported with its line
a row for a region outside the plan is reported with its line
a budget of zero is allowed
a budget written as "1,200" is reported as not a number
a year before the plan's first year is outside the plan
every row of a repeated year and region is reported, not only the later one
a missing year and region is reported even when a duplicate keeps the row count right

origin.section: Check Every Row Before the Model Sees It, One Mask per Rule

concepts: each data rule is one boolean mask, and every row a mask marks is reported with its line
